---
title: "Series and parallel resistance"
subtitle: "Electrical engineering basics"
toc: true
---

## Series

Resistors in series share the same current, and their voltage drops add — so resistance simply sums:

$$
R_{series} = R_1 + R_2 + R_3
$$

## Parallel

Resistors in parallel share the same voltage, and their currents add, giving a reciprocal sum:

$$
\frac{1}{R_{parallel}} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2} + \frac{1}{R_3}
$$

The parallel combination is always smaller than the smallest individual resistor — adding a path for current can only make it easier for current to flow.

## Calculator

Leave a value at 0 to exclude that resistor (treated as not present).

```{=html}
<div id="rseries-calc"></div>
<script src="../assets/js/calc-engine.js"></script>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "rseries-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "R1", label: "R1 (Ω)", value: 100, min: 0, step: 1 },
    { id: "R2", label: "R2 (Ω)", value: 220, min: 0, step: 1 },
    { id: "R3", label: "R3 (Ω)", value: 0, min: 0, step: 1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "series", label: "R series" },
    { id: "parallel", label: "R parallel" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    var rs = [v.R1, v.R2, v.R3].filter(function (r) { return r > 0; });
    if (rs.length === 0) return { series: "-", parallel: "-" };
    var sum = rs.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + b; }, 0);
    var invSum = rs.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + 1 / b; }, 0);
    var par = invSum > 0 ? 1 / invSum : 0;
    return {
      series: sum.toFixed(2) + " Ω",
      parallel: par.toFixed(2) + " Ω"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
